data.title: Torque Frenzy!
data.solution:
initial_torque = int(input())
n_commands = int(input())
input_stream = input().split()

k = c = 0

final_torque = initial_torque

for cmd in input_stream:
    if cmd == '1':
        k = 0
        c += 1
        final_torque *= (1+c*.1) #increase by 10% * counter[c]
    elif cmd == '-1':
        c  = 0
        k += 1
        final_torque *= (1-k*.1) #decrease by 10% * counter[k]
    else:
        k = c = 0
        final_torque *= .95 #decrease by 5%
        
print(f'{final_torque:.2f}') # rounded to decimal places

• Otherwise, increase the [[counter]] by {{1}}.

•  {{1}} → <<Press the wheel>>. Update [[torque]] = [[torque]] × (1 + 0.1 × [[counter]]).
• {{-1}} → <<Reverse press>>. Update [[torque]] = [[torque]] × (1 - 0.1 × [[counter]]).
•  {{0}} → <<Neutral>>. Update [[torque]] = [[torque]] × 0.95.

Given an [[initial_torque]], [[n_commands]] and [[input_stream]], compute the [[final_torque]]  after processing all commands.

Output the result <<rounded to 2 decimal places>>.

Keep your wheel under control!

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A wheel maintains both a counter (with an initial value of 0) and a torque (with an initial value of initial_torque). The wheel reacts to a stream of commands.

For each command:
• If the current command is the first command or is different from the previous command, set the counter to 1.
• Otherwise, increase the counter by 1.
• After updating the counter value, update the torque value according to the current command:

• 1 → Press the wheel. Update torque = torque × (1 + 0.1 × counter).
• -1 → Reverse press. Update torque = torque × (1 - 0.1 × counter).
• 0 → Neutral. Update torque = torque × 0.95.

Given an initial_torque, n_commands and input_stream, compute the final_torque after processing all commands.

Output the result rounded to 2 decimal places.

Keep your wheel under control!
Input
Line 1: initial_torque, an integer for the initial torque.
Line 2: n_commands, an integer for the number of commands in the stream.
Line 3: input_stream, a string containing -1's, 0's and 1's with space in between.
Output
Line 1: final_torque, final torque rounded to 2 decimal places.
Constraints
0 ≤ initial_torque ≤ 1000
0 ≤ n_commands ≤ 50
0 ≤ final_torque ≤ 10000
Example
Input
100
5
1 1 0 0 -1
Output
107.22
